summary:
I checked this repository before changing anything.

**The requested change is frontend-only.** "Change the health status text in the footer to green when the API is ok and red when it is not" is a styling/binding change in the Angular footer (`app.component.html` / `.css` in `realworld-app-angular-v20`) — there is nothing in a .NET API that can colour text, and faking it here (e.g. returning a colour field the contract doesn't have) would be inventing contract the other side didn't ask for.

**The backend side of the contract is already in place**, spelled exactly as the contract requires, from the earlier `a8e86da2e5ea` correction:

- `src/CleanArchitecture.Api/Controllers/HealthController.cs:8` — `[Route("api/health")] [AllowAnonymous]`, `GET` returning `Ok(new HealthResponse("ok"))`.
- `src/CleanArchitecture.Contracts/Common/HealthResponse.cs:3` — `record HealthResponse(string Status)`, serialized by ASP.NET Core's default camelCase policy as `{"status":"ok"}` — which is what the footer needs to read `API: ok` and to distinguish ok from not-ok.
- `tests/CleanArchitecture.Api.IntegrationTests/Controllers/HealthControllerTests.cs` — asserts 200 and `status == "ok"` anonymously.

So every item on this side was already true, and I made no edits. Project rules applied: route spelled `api/health` to match the existing `api/tutorials` convention, and the response field kept as `status` so the two sides agree.

The colouring (green when `status` is `ok`, red on `unavailable`/error) is left for the frontend repository `realworld-app-angular-v20`.
